concerns.text: Both T007a and T007b are marked [P] but each writes to the same file `code/data_loader.py`. Running them in parallel can cause race conditions or overwritten code. Either remove the [P] tag or split the implementation into separate, sequential steps.
T003 and T003a both modify `code/config.py` and are marked [P] despite a direct dependency (T003 depends on T003a). Parallel execution would corrupt the config file; the [P] tag is unsafe here.

T050a (annotation tool implementation) and T050c (synthetic placeholder generation) both edit `code/annotation_tool.py` and are marked [P]. Since they target the same file, they cannot safely run in parallel; the [P] tag should be removed.

T032 (resource monitoring report) and T032b (runtime/RSS constraint check) both modify `code/monitor_resources.py` and are marked [P]. Parallel execution would lead to conflicting edits; the parallel‑safe flag is incorrect.

User Story 2 tasks (Phase 4) depend on artifacts produced by User Story 1 (e.g., `data/derived/stress_curves.parquet` from T015a). This violates the independent‑shippable unit principle: each story should be testable end‑to‑end without requiring another story’s outputs.

User Story 3 tasks depend on collapse‑point artifacts from User Story 2 (`data/derived/collapse_points.parquet` from T022a) and on human‑annotation artifacts from User Story 1/2. Hence US3 is not independently implementable, breaching the user‑story independence requirement.

T009 is a unit test for T012 but is listed under Phase 2 with a comment “Moved to Phase 3”. Its placement before the dependent implementation (Phase 3) creates a producer‑before‑consumer ordering issue.

T012c creates `code/data_loader.py` and `code/distortion_engine.py` functions, while T012b adds a new module `code/realism_validator.py` that depends on the output of T012c. Both are marked [P] but T012b depends on T012c, so they cannot safely run in parallel.
